content:
The image shows a soybean stem split open longitudinally, revealing **brown/tan discoloration of the internal pith tissue**. The exterior stem appears green and healthy. This is a classic diagnostic technique — splitting the stem to observe pith color.

Key observations:
- Brown/orange-tan discoloration throughout the pith
- Stem exterior still green
- No white pith (rules out SDS)

The Brown Stem Rot reference images confirm the pattern — split stems showing internal tissue discoloration. The test image matches perfectly:

- **Test image**: Split stem with clear brown/tan pith discoloration — the exact diagnostic technique for Brown Stem Rot
- **Reference BSR images**: Show split stems with pith browning, plus interveinal chlorosis on leaves
- The brown pith (not white) specifically distinguishes Brown Stem Rot from Sudden Death Syndrome
